lead: Spain’s most cycling-friendly city awaits: almost 200 km of cycle lanes, completely flat terrain and the Turia Gardens as a green motorway crossing the city from end to end.
Explore Valencia at your own pace on your own bike for 24 hours or with an audio guide included.

items.title: Bike hire in Valencia
items.subtitle: No guide · At your own pace · ~200 km of cycle lanes · 10% off with VTC · Rated 5/5
items.body: The freest way to discover Valencia: hire a bike for 24 hours and explore the city entirely at your own pace. Valencia is one of the most “bike-friendly” cities in Spain, with almost 200 kilometres of cycle lanes that run through the historic centre, the Turia Gardens, the City of Arts and Sciences, the seafront promenade and the beach. Valencia’s mild climate lets you enjoy cycling practically any day of the year. The operator DoYouBike manages the hire with well-maintained bikes equipped with what you need for the city. Ideal for travellers who prefer to explore on their own with total freedom over timetables and routes.

items.title: Bike hire with audio guide included
items.subtitle: Audio guide in 3 languages · No in-person guide · At your own pace · 10% off with VTC
items.body: The perfect option for those who want the freedom to explore without a guide but with all of Valencia’s cultural and historical context in their ear. The hire includes the bike for 8 to 10 hours and a downloadable audio guide available in Spanish, English and Italian, developed by Flight Mode. The audio guide lays out a self-guided route through the most interesting points of the city — the historic centre, the Turia Gardens, El Carmen district, the City of Arts and Sciences — with precise explanations at each stop. No fixed timetables, no groups, no waiting. You set the pace.

items.title: Bike hire and boat trip on the Albufera
items.subtitle: Cycle route to the Albufera · Traditional boat trip on the lake · Nature and rice fields
items.body: A unique combination that blends the pleasure of cycling with the most authentic Albufera experience: the traditional boat trip on the lake and the canals among the rice fields. The cycling route leaves from Valencia and follows the tracks that lead to the Albufera Natural Park, the largest lake in Spain and the birthplace of Valencian paella. On reaching the jetty, a traditional boat tours the lake and its canals while the guide explains the history and nature of the park. A 4-hour experience that combines nature, local culture and a unique Mediterranean landscape. Available every day with departure at 10:00.

items.title: Valencia Open Bike Tour
items.subtitle: Guide in English and Dutch · Every day · Bike included · 10% off with VTC
items.body: Valencia’s highest-rated bike tour, with a perfect 5/5 score. An expert guide leads the 3-hour route through the city’s most emblematic corners and most authentic neighbourhoods. The Valencia Open Bike Tour covers the historic centre, the Turia Gardens — the longest linear park in Spain, laid out in the old riverbed —, the Ruzafa district, the City of Arts and Sciences and the seafront promenade with views of the Mediterranean. The tour gives a complete perspective on Valencia: the medieval city, the Modernista city, the cutting-edge city and the coastal city, all in a single three-hour ride that adapts to the group’s pace.

items.title: Guided bike tour of València with horchata and fartons tasting
items.subtitle: Historic centre · Turia Gardens · Horchata and fartons tasting included · Monday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday
items.body: A bike tour of Valencia that combines the city’s most emblematic landscapes and monuments with an authentic tasting of horchata de chufa and fartons, the quintessential Valencian snack. The 3-hour route crosses the historic centre and its medieval squares, rides along the Turia Gardens and stops at a traditional horchatería to enjoy the freshest horchata in the city. Available on Mondays, Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays with a guide in Spanish and English. An experience that blends Valencian culture, architecture, nature and gastronomy in a single ride.

items.title: Guided bike route to the Albufera with horchata and fartons
items.subtitle: Cycle route to the Albufera · Horchata and fartons · Guide · 10% off with VTC · Rated 5/5
items.body: The most complete bike route from Valencia: 4 and a half hours that take the cyclist from the heart of the city to the Albufera Natural Park, with a stop to taste horchata de chufa and fartons along the way. The route follows the cycle lanes of the Turia Gardens and the tracks around the lake, with views of the rice fields and the park’s rich birdlife. Along the way the guide explains the history of the lake, rice growing and the relationship between the Albufera and Valencian paella. Available on Tuesdays and Thursdays, departing at 09:30. Completely flat terrain suitable for all levels.

items.subtitle: Whole city · CAC · Turia Gardens · Beach · Every day at 11:00
items.body: A guided bike ride through Valencia’s most iconic spots, with a daily departure at 11:00. The 3-hour tour covers the city’s great attractions in a balanced route between history, modernity and coast: the historic centre and its medieval squares, the Turia Gardens, the City of Arts and Sciences with its spectacular Calatrava buildings and the seafront promenade with views of the Mediterranean. Available in Spanish and Dutch with a local guide. Suitable for all levels, as Valencia is a completely flat city with an extensive network of cycle lanes separated from traffic.

blocks.title: Tips for getting around Valencia by bike
items: The Turia Gardens are Valencia’s prettiest cycling route: 9 km of linear park linking the historic centre with the City of Arts and Sciences without a single traffic light
If you want to cycle to the beach, the easiest way is to follow the Turia to its end and continue along the seafront promenade to Las Arenas or Malvarrosa
To reach the Albufera from the centre it is about 12–15 km along flat tracks among rice fields; the guided tours include the bike and know the best traffic-free routes
With the Valencia Tourist Card you get 10% off most bike hires and tours at visitvalencia.com
The Valenbisi system (municipal public bike) has more than 270 stations: perfect for short trips and available with a credit card without an annual subscription
Best time for tours: early in the morning (9–11 h) to avoid the summer heat and the tourist groups in the historic centre
